target.title: feat: add tools.fs.roots — per-agent filesystem roots with access modes
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: `tools.fs.workspaceOnly` is binary, so operators cannot safely allow agents to read or write a specific host path outside the workspace without opening broader filesystem access.
- Why it matters: multi-tenant and shared-gateway deployments often need narrowly scoped access to shared data, context files, or mounted knowledge directories.
- What changed: added `tools.fs.roots`, an explicit allowlist of filesystem roots with per-root `kind` (`dir`/`file`) and `access` (`ro`/`rw`), wired through host-mode FS tools, `apply_patch`, local media loading, outbound local-media/reply-delivery paths, and prompt-image auto-load.
- Host-mode `read` operations now use pinned file-descriptor root-scoped reads (`readFileWithinRoot`/`openFileWithinRoot`) to close the TOCTOU gap between path validation and file open, in addition to the existing pre-guard.
- Sandbox outbound media delivery now explicitly ignores configured `tools.fs.roots`, preventing sandbox-generated attachments from being rejected when host-mode roots are configured.
- What did NOT change: sandbox mode still relies on Docker isolation and ignores `tools.fs.roots`; `exec` sandboxing is unchanged; `tools.allow` / `tools.deny` behavior is unchanged.

## Change Type (select all)

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [x] Docs
- [x] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [x] Integrations
- [x] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #
- Related #
- [ ] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause / Regression History (if applicable)

- Root cause: existing FS policy exposed only two modes for host paths: workspace-only or unrestricted.
- Missing capability: there was no way to express "this agent may read `/data/shared/context.md` but may not read the rest of the host".
- Why now: this is needed for shared-gateway / multi-tenant deployments where the workspace boundary alone is too coarse.
- If unknown, what was ruled out: sandbox mode stays out of scope because sandbox tools resolve container paths, not host paths, and partial host-path enforcement there would create an inconsistent security model.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should catch this:
  - [x] Unit test
  - [x] Seam / integration test
  - [ ] End-to-end test
  - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient
- Target tests/files:
  - `src/agents/tool-fs-policy.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/pi-tools.multi-root-guard.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/pi-tools.sandbox-mounted-paths.workspace-only.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/pi-tools.workspace-only-false.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/apply-patch.test.ts`
  - `src/media/local-roots.test.ts`
  - `src/media/load-options.test.ts`
  - `src/media/local-media-access.test.ts`
  - `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-media-paths.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/run/images.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/tools/image-tool.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/tools/image-generate-tool.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/tools/pdf-tool.test.ts`
  - `src/infra/outbound/deliver.test.ts`
  - `src/infra/fs-safe.test.ts`
  - `src/infra/fs-pinned-write-helper.spawn-error.test.ts`
  - `src/infra/fs-safe.unlink-helper-error.test.ts`
  - `extensions/googlechat/src/actions.test.ts`
  - `extensions/googlechat/src/channel.test.ts`
  - `extensions/feishu/src/media.test.ts`
  - `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/reply-delivery.test.ts`
- Scenarios locked in:
  - lexical dir/file root matching and ro/rw enforcement
  - canonical-root precedence over alias roots for host-mode mutation paths
  - unlink/delete behavior preserving symlink-entry semantics while still respecting stricter canonical roots
  - roots precedence over `workspaceOnly` for host-mode FS access
  - sandbox-mode fallback still honoring `workspaceOnly`
  - rooted local image/PDF/reference-image loads outside the workspace
  - rooted outbound local-media and reply-delivery paths preserving file-vs-dir root semantics
  - rooted prompt-image auto-load outside the workspace
  - host-mode reads use pinned-FD root-scoped operations (TOCTOU-safe)
  - sandboxed outbound media delivery ignores configured host roots
  - rooted delete helper gracefully falls back when pinned write helper spawn fails
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: the risky surfaces here are policy resolution, host-path mutation, and media path propagation, so targeted seam tests catch the actual failure modes without requiring a full live deployment.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- New config surface: `tools.fs.roots` on global `tools.fs` and per-agent `tools.fs`.
- Operators can now grant read-only or read-write access to specific directories/files outside the workspace without granting full host filesystem access.
- Host-mode `read` / `write` / `edit` / `apply_patch` now respect those explicit roots.
- Local media loading, outbound local-media/reply-delivery flows, and prompt-image auto-load now preserve and enforce rooted file/dir access semantics.
- When both `roots` and `workspaceOnly` are set, `roots` takes precedence for host-mode FS access and a warning is logged.

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`Yes/No`) Yes
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- New/changed network calls? (`Yes/No`) No
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- Data access scope changed? (`Yes/No`) Yes
- If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation:
  - This adds a new operator-controlled path restriction model for host-mode FS access. Risk is policy misunderstanding or incomplete enforcement across FS-adjacent surfaces. Mitigation: all configured roots are validated as absolute paths; enforcement is alias-safe; canonical root precedence is preserved for host-mode mutation paths; host-mode `read`/`write`/`edit`/`apply_patch`, local media inputs, outbound local-media/reply-delivery, and prompt-image auto-load are covered; host-mode reads use pinned-FD root-scoped operations to close TOCTOU gaps; sandbox mode explicitly ignores roots to avoid host/container path confusion.

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: macOS 15 / darwin 25.3.0
- Runtime/container: local repo checkout
- Model/provider: N/A for core FS policy; targeted local media tests use mocked image/PDF/image-generation providers
- Integration/channel (if any): host-mode FS tools + local media loading + outbound local-media reply flows
- Relevant config (redacted):

```json5
{
  "tools": {
    "fs": {
      "roots": [
        { "path": "/opt/app/workspaces/agent-1", "kind": "dir", "access": "rw" },
        { "path": "/data/finance/invoices", "kind": "dir", "access": "ro" },
        { "path": "/data/finance/context.md", "kind": "file", "access": "ro" }
      ]
    }

}
```

### Steps

1. Configure an agent with `tools.fs.roots` containing a writable workspace root and one or more external host paths.
2. Attempt `read`/`write`/`edit`/`apply_patch` and local media access both inside and outside those roots.
3. Attempt outbound local-media / reply-delivery flows with both dir roots and exact file roots.
4. Attempt prompt-image auto-load from a rooted external image path.
5. Attempt the same config in sandbox mode.

### Expected

- Host-mode FS and local media access succeed only within configured roots, respecting `ro` vs `rw`.
- Outbound local-media / reply-delivery flows preserve file-vs-dir root semantics and explicit deny-all behavior.
- Prompt-image auto-load accepts explicitly rooted host paths.
- Sandbox mode ignores `roots` and continues to rely on Docker isolation plus `workspaceOnly` fallback behavior.

### Actual

- Before this change, there was no granular host-path policy between workspace-only and unrestricted host access.

## Evidence

Attach at least one:

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [ ] Trace/log snippets
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

## Human Verification (required)

- Additional focused regressions were exercised during review for:

## Review Conversations

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes/No`) Yes

## Failure Recovery (if this breaks)

- How to disable/revert this change quickly: remove `tools.fs.roots` from config or revert this PR.
- Files/config to restore: `src/agents/pi-tools.ts`, `src/agents/tool-fs-policy.ts`, `src/agents/pi-tools.multi-root-guard.ts`, `src/agents/apply-patch.ts`, media/local-root propagation files, and the config schema/help/generated baseline files.
- Known bad symptoms reviewers should watch for: host-mode local media or prompt-image access unexpectedly denied for paths inside configured roots, rooted outbound attachments unexpectedly losing exact-file semantics, symlink delete/unlink behavior regressing at root boundaries, or sandbox-generated outbound attachments unexpectedly blocked when host-mode `tools.fs.roots` is configured.

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: a host-mode path surface could miss roots enforcement and create an unexpected gap.
  - Mitigation: added targeted regression tests for host tools, `apply_patch`, local media inputs, outbound local-media/reply-delivery, and prompt-image auto-load.
- Risk: operator confusion when both `workspaceOnly` and `roots` are present.
  - Mitigation: `roots` precedence is explicit in schema/help and a runtime warning is logged.
- Risk: `exec` still bypasses FS roots through shell commands.
  - Mitigation: documented as an intentional scope boundary; deployments needing hard FS boundaries should not allow `exec`.

## AI assistance

- [x] AI-assisted
- Testing: locally revalidated on the current merged head (`7b771d448d`) with `pnpm check`, focused media/WhatsApp review-thread regressions, and the two prior PR-specific filtered tests; full `pnpm test` and `pnpm build` were not rerun on this final merged head; GitHub CI is green on `7b771d448d` (74 successful, 9 skipped) after the latest review fix.




## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** `tools.fs.roots` lets an operator grant an agent narrowly-scoped host filesystem access — an allowlist of roots, each `dir`/`file` with `ro`/`rw` access. Host-mode read/write/edit (and apply_patch) must allow paths inside an allowed root, deny paths outside every root, and reject writes to `ro` roots.
- **Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw checkout at PR head `b4056fc332` (Node 22, macOS), driving the production host-mode filesystem tools against a real on-disk temporary directory tree (real `fs` syscalls; no fixtures or stubs).
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Created a real temp tree (an `rw` root `shared-rw`, an `ro` root `shared-ro`, and a `secret/` directory outside every root with a real file in it), built the production tool set via `createOpenClawCodingTools({ config: { tools: { fs: { roots: [...] } } } })`, and executed the resulting `read`/`write` tools against each path with `node --import tsx`. Live console output below.
- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
config tools.fs.roots:
  - { path: /tmp/fs-roots-proof-qTDt3u/shared-rw, kind: dir, access: rw }
  - { path: /tmp/fs-roots-proof-qTDt3u/shared-ro, kind: dir, access: ro }
workspace (not a root): /tmp/fs-roots-proof-qTDt3u/workspace
forbidden dir (not a root): /tmp/fs-roots-proof-qTDt3u/secret

=== host-mode reads ===
READ  inside rw root  (shared-rw/notes.txt)
      -> ALLOWED, content: "rw-root content"
READ  inside ro root  (shared-ro/policy.txt)
      -> ALLOWED, content: "ro-root content"
READ  OUTSIDE roots   (secret/passwords.txt)
      -> DENIED: Access denied: path '/tmp/fs-roots-proof-qTDt3u/secret/passwords.txt' is outside allowed filesystem roots

=== host-mode writes ===
WRITE inside rw root  (shared-rw/created.txt)
      -> ALLOWED, on disk: true
WRITE inside ro root  (shared-ro/hack.txt)
      -> DENIED: Access denied: path '/tmp/fs-roots-proof-qTDt3u/shared-ro/hack.txt' is inside read-only root '/tmp/fs-roots-proof-qTDt3u/shared-ro'  (on disk: false)
WRITE OUTSIDE roots   (secret/exfil.txt)
      -> DENIED: Access denied: path '/tmp/fs-roots-proof-qTDt3u/secret/exfil.txt' is outside allowed filesystem roots  (on disk: false)

verify: secret/passwords.txt still says: "TOP SECRET — outside every allowed root"
```

- **Observed result after fix:** Reads inside the `rw` and `ro` roots returned the real file contents. A read of `secret/passwords.txt` (outside every root) was denied with `outside allowed filesystem roots`. A write inside the `rw` root landed on disk (`on disk: true`); a write to the `ro` root was denied (`inside read-only root`) and a write outside every root was denied — both left nothing on disk (`on disk: false`), and the out-of-root secret file was byte-for-byte unchanged afterward.
- **What was not tested:** Sandbox mode is out of scope by design — sandbox ignores `tools.fs.roots` and relies on Docker isolation — so it was not exercised here. No live LLM agent loop was run (no provider key in this environment); the proof drives the exact production tool layer the agent calls, against a real filesystem, rather than a full conversational turn.

target.title: fix: surface terminal agent run failures
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An embedded agent can reach a terminal failure while returning no visible payload. The reply operation records the failure, but the normal chat path previously had nothing to send, so an interactive request could appear to be ignored.

## Why This Change Was Made

The contributor patch correctly identified the missing presentation, but its early `kind: "final"` returns bypassed pending tool/block drains, reply normalization, dedupe, session bookkeeping, and usage/model metadata.

This rewrite carries a prepared terminal-failure payload through the existing success-shaped run result. The outer reply owner waits for pending delivery, evaluates the canonical side-effect and source-delivery evidence, then appends the failure only when nothing was already delivered. Existing visible errors, message-tool/source replies, block streams, cron/approval side effects, non-direct silent policy, and heartbeat-specific copy remain authoritative.

## User Impact

Interactive terminal run failures now produce one safe visible failure instead of silence. A reply already delivered through another supported path is not duplicated, and heartbeat failures retain heartbeat-specific guidance.

Release note context: Fix interactive requests appearing to be ignored when an agent run ends in a terminal failure without a visible payload.

## Evidence

- Testbox `tbx_01kwsmzw7a12qk14aezg1w0wbr` on the final rebased head:
  - 229 focused execution tests passed.
  - 67 payload normalization/threading tests passed.
  - 71 full `runReplyAgent` E2E tests passed.
  - Exact eight-file `check:changed` core/coreTests/docs gate passed, including core/test typechecks, lint, import-cycle and repository guards.
- E2E regression proof holds a pending tool-result delivery open, confirms the reply does not finish early, releases it, and then observes exactly one marked generic failure.
- Negative E2E coverage proves both message-tool and source-reply delivery suppress the duplicate.
- Reply-threading coverage proves filtered payloads cannot consume `replyToMode: first`, enabled display lanes share the slot, and message-tool dedupe sees the final routed target.
- Unit coverage includes exhausted, completed, and heartbeat terminal results plus preservation of existing visible terminal payloads.

## What Problem This Solves

Group-channel messages need a generic way to distinguish the runtime message author from the operator/user represented by the agent session. Without source actor attribution, downstream prompts, tools, and memory adapters can only see channel/session context and may conflate another group participant with the operator. This should be solved as a channel contract, not as a deployment-specific memory backend workaround.

## Summary

- Adds a generic `SourceActor` inbound context contract for the runtime identity of the message author.
- Maps Signal sender identity into `SourceActor` without making the contract Signal-specific.
- Types `SourceActorRole` as `operator | participant | self | system | external`.
- Documents `SourceActor` as canonical and the flattened `SourceActor*` fields as scalar mirrors for prompt templates.

Closes #100423

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running `openclaw sandbox explain --agent <id>` with `workspaceAccess: "rw"` would see `workspaceRoot` reported as the configured sandbox root even though sandbox commands write through the agent workspace mounted at `/workspace`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The sandbox workspace path selection is now shared between runtime setup and `sandbox explain`, and the explain output includes the effective host workspace, configured sandbox root, container workdir, workspace source, and Docker mount table. This is a diagnostics-only change; it does not change sandbox creation or mount behavior.

## User Impact

Users can now rely on `sandbox explain` to find where files actually land for `rw` workspaces instead of looking under the configured sandbox root by mistake.

## Evidence

Before: on `upstream/main`, `src/commands/sandbox-explain.ts` set `sandbox.workspaceRoot` directly from `sandboxCfg.workspaceRoot`, while `src/agents/sandbox/context.ts` selected the agent workspace as `workspaceDir` when `workspaceAccess === "rw"`.

target.title: fix(ios): defer QR pairing after scanner dismissal
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #99571.

Fixes an issue where iOS users scanning a gateway pairing QR could have the scanner dismiss at the wrong time, lose the trust/approval handoff, or crash while VisionKit was still stopping camera capture.

The affected surfaces are the iOS onboarding scanner, Gateway Settings scanner, app/open-url setup-link handling, and post-scan gateway approval handoff.

## Why This Change Was Made

The scanner now stops VisionKit scanning, queues one typed QR/setup result, dismisses the scanner sheet, and processes pairing only from the sheet dismissal path after a short main-actor settling delay. The final branch also handles setup links delivered during app/onboarding launch by staging UIKit app-delegate URLs through the same gateway setup-link path used by SwiftUI `.onOpenURL`.

This keeps the scanner lifecycle separate from gateway trust UI and avoids re-entering the onboarding/settings presentation stack while VisionKit is still dismissing.

## User Impact

iOS users can pair a gateway by scanning a QR code from onboarding or from Settings without losing the approval flow. After approval, the app reaches Chat and can send/receive messages immediately.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(agents): surface real plugin approval rejection reason to agent
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #100212: When the gateway rejects a plugin approval request (e.g. schema validation → `INVALID_REQUEST`), the agent receives a hardcoded "Plugin approval required (gateway unavailable)" message. The gateway is actually healthy and actively rejected the request — the misleading message points debugging in the wrong direction.

**Real-world impact**: This misled operators at Clawnify.com during a production incident where an overlong approval title (98 chars, cap is 80) caused every mutating tool call to fail. The agent, seeing "gateway unavailable," concluded the target app was broken — while the gateway was perfectly healthy.

## Why This Change Was Made

The catch block around the `plugin.approval.request` gateway call in `src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.ts` returned a fixed string regardless of error type. Now we distinguish:

- **GatewayClientRequestError** (gateway code present) → `"Plugin approval request rejected: <real message>"` — gateway is up, request was invalid
- **Other errors** (connection refused, timeout, etc.) → `"Plugin approval required (gateway unavailable)"` — genuine transport failure

## User Impact

- Agents and operators now see the real rejection reason, enabling faster root-cause analysis
- Gateway-unavailability detection still works correctly for actual transport failures
- Backward compatible: all existing tests pass unchanged

## Evidence

- [x] Source-repro: `agent-tools.before-tool-call.ts:931-935` verified as the single hardcoded-message site
- [x] `pnpm test src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.embedded-mode.test.ts` — 15 tests pass
- [x] `pnpm test src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.e2e.test.ts` — 58 tests pass
- [x] `oxlint` passes on changed file

target.title: fix: media replies fail after prompt lock release
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users sending multiple visible message-tool media replies could see the embedded agent fail with `session file changed while embedded prompt lock was released` after the media had already been delivered.

The affected workflow is embedded agent delivery through channel message tools, especially batched image/media sends that mirror visible deliveries into the session transcript while the prompt lock is released.

## Why This Change Was Made

Prompt-lock recovery already preserves delivery mirror transcript appends, but the recovery classifier did not recognize side-append `leaf` controls written with those mirrors. This change treats only structurally valid `appendMode: "side"` leaf controls as prompt-released opaque entries so SessionManager can merge the delivery side branch, while active leaf controls remain takeover-triggering edits.

## User Impact

Users can receive batched media replies without the agent falsely reporting a session takeover during cleanup. The session takeover fence still rejects prompt-affecting branch changes and malformed leaf controls.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.session-lock.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose` passed, 110 tests.
- `pnpm build` passed after adding the redacted prompt-release proof logs.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local` passed with no accepted/actionable findings after the active-leaf guard was tightened.
- Live local proof on fixed gateway `2026.7.1-beta.1 (5c30bcf)`, 2026-07-05 02:14 Asia/Shanghai, redacted Weixin direct chat:
  - `message` tool started batched visible media sends at 02:14:20.
  - 11 local image uploads were attempted: 5 `hilton-*` images and 6 `yatu-*` images.
  - 11 `sendImageMessageWeixin: success` entries were logged between 02:14:21 and 02:14:27.
  - `prompt-released session change merged` was logged repeatedly during those media deliveries, showing prompt-released transcript changes were merged instead of treated as takeover.
  - `embedded run agent end ... isError=false` and `message processed ... outcome=completed` were logged at 02:14:30-02:14:31.
  - No new `session file changed while embedded prompt lock was released` or `EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError` entries appeared during the fixed-gateway test window; the only matching entries in the same local log were from the pre-fix npm-global run at 01:03.

target.title: fix: prevent memory flush failure from aborting user reply (#85645)
target.body:
## Summary

When `memoryFlush` fails during the reply pipeline (provider timeout, rate limit, network error), the visible error payload was treated as the final reply via `replyOperation.fail("run_failed", ...)`. This aborted the user's actual message. Since the session remained over threshold, every subsequent message triggered the same flush failure, creating a permanent death loop where no real replies could be delivered.

## Changes

**`src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.ts`**
- Memory flush visible error payloads are now logged via `logVerbose()` and **not** delivered as the reply. The main reply run proceeds normally.
- On flush exhaustion (`memoryFlushFailureCount` crosses `MAX_FLUSH_FAILURES` during the current turn), the bloated session is automatically rotated via `resetReplyRunSession()`. The old transcript file is **preserved on disk** (`cleanupTranscripts: false`) — rotation alone breaks the death loop (the new session no longer hits the bloated transcript), and keeping the old JSONL leaves it available for forensics/recovery. The active session only replays recent turns regardless of this flag.
- Added an **opt-in, non-terminal degraded notice**: when `agents.defaults.compaction.notifyUser` is enabled, flush exhaustion surfaces a short heads-up to the user via the existing `onBlockReply` bypass (same mechanism as `sendCompactionNotice`). It **never** calls `replyOperation.fail()` and **never** aborts the reply. Default (`notifyUser=false`) keeps the silent log-and-continue behavior. No new config surface is added.
- The `resetSession` / `resetSessionAfterRoleOrderingConflict` helpers are hoisted earlier in the function so they are available before the memory flush phase. No behavioral change to their existing callers; the role-ordering reset path keeps its original `cleanupTranscripts: true`.

**`src/auto-reply/reply/session.ts`**
- `initSessionState()` now clears `memoryFlushFailureCount`, `memoryFlushLastFailedAt`, and `memoryFlushLastFailureError` when a session is reset (e.g., via `/new`), preventing stale failure state from carrying over.

**`src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-session-reset.ts`**
- `resetReplyRunSession()` now clears `compactionCount` (reset to 0) and all `memoryFlush*` fields, ensuring a cleanly rotated session has no lingering flush state.

## What is NOT changed

- `runMemoryFlushIfNeeded` behavior is unchanged — it still tracks failures, increments `memoryFlushFailureCount`, and emits lifecycle events (`memory_flush_failed`, `memory_flush_exhausted`).
- `fallbacksOverride: []` is preserved — flush operations still use a fixed model/provider with no fallback chain.
- `MAX_FLUSH_FAILURES = 3` threshold is unchanged.
- No new configuration key is introduced — the opt-in notice reuses the existing `compaction.notifyUser` gate.

## Tests

- **`agent-runner-direct-runtime-config.test.ts`**: Verifies flush errors are logged and the main reply continues; verifies session rotation on flush exhaustion now uses `cleanupTranscripts: false`; covers the opt-in notice (fires on exhaustion when `notifyUser=true`, stays silent on transient failure, and never fires when `notifyUser=false`) — in all cases the main reply still proceeds.
- **`agent-runner-session-reset.test.ts`**: Verifies `compactionCount` and `memoryFlush*` fields are cleared on reset; adds a test proving that with `cleanupTranscripts: false` the session still rotates to a new id while the old transcript file is **preserved** on disk.
- **`session.test.ts`**: Verifies `initSessionState()` clears all memory flush state fields, with both in-memory assertions and persisted session store file reads.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: When `memoryFlush` / auto-compaction fails permanently (provider timeout, rate limit, 5xx), current `main` routes the visible flush error into `replyOperation.fail("run_failed")` before the main reply run, aborting the user's real reply. Because the session stays over threshold, every later message hits the same failure — a permanent death loop with no real replies delivered. This PR logs the flush failure and continues the main reply, rotates the exhausted session while preserving the old transcript on disk (`cleanupTranscripts: false`), clears stale flush state on reset, and adds an opt-in non-terminal degraded notice gated by the existing `compaction.notifyUser`.
- **Real environment tested**: OpenClaw Gateway run directly from this PR's source at current head `5dc502d76f` (branch `fix/memory-flush-death-loop-85645`) via `tsx` (`node --import tsx src/index.ts gateway run`), on macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0. Isolated state dir, `auth: none`, Gateway port `14881`. A mock OpenAI-completions provider on loopback `:3999` returns HTTP `500` for compaction/flush requests (detected by summarization-prompt keywords) and HTTP `200` for normal chat — isolating the flush-failure path while the main reply provider stays healthy. Config: `softThresholdTokens: 800`, `contextWindow: 4096`, `maxTokens: 1024`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  1. Start the mock provider: `node mock-provider/server.mjs` (loopback `:3999`, returns 500 on flush requests, 200 on normal chat).
  2. Start the Gateway from this PR's source at head `5dc502d76f`: `node --import tsx src/index.ts gateway --force --port 14881 --auth none run` with an isolated state dir.
  3. Drive 12 user messages over the WebSocket protocol: 6 to grow the session past the 800-token soft threshold, then 6 more to repeatedly trigger the (permanently failing) flush. Wait for each `agent.wait` completion.
- **Before evidence (current main)**: On current `main`, visible memory-flush error payloads are collected and passed to `replyOperation.fail("run_failed")` before the main reply run, so the user's real reply is aborted and subsequent messages repeat the failure (`src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.ts` flush-error path on `main`).
- **Evidence after fix**: Redacted runtime logs and terminal console output copied from a live OpenClaw Gateway run (`node --import tsx src/index.ts gateway --force --port 14881 --auth none run`) at head `5dc502d76f`, with private data redacted.

  Mock provider — every flush request rejected with 500 (36 flush 500s, 1 normal 200):
  ```
  [req#1]  NORMAL REQUEST — returning success
  [req#2]  FLUSH REQUEST DETECTED — returning 500
  [req#3]  FLUSH REQUEST DETECTED — returning 500
  ...
  (36 flush requests total, all returned HTTP 500)
  ```

  Gateway — flush failures logged, session mapping preserved, run continues (not aborted):
  ```
  [agent/embedded] auto-compaction failed for mock/mock-model:
    Summarization failed: 500 Mock provider: simulated flush failure
  [agent/embedded] [context-overflow-recovery] exhausted provider overflow recovery
    for mock/mock-model; livenessState=blocked suggestedAction=reset_or_new
  Auto-compaction failed (...). Preserving existing session mapping for [SESSION].
  ```

  WebSocket client — all 12 messages received a reply (`status=ok`), none aborted:
  ```
  [MSG-1]      agent done: status=ok
  [MSG-2]      agent done: status=ok
  [MSG-3]      agent done: status=ok
  [MSG-4]      agent done: status=ok
  [MSG-5]      agent done: status=ok
  [MSG-6]      agent done: status=ok
  [TRIGGER-7]  agent done: status=ok
  [TRIGGER-8]  agent done: status=ok
  [TRIGGER-9]  agent done: status=ok
  [TRIGGER-10] agent done: status=ok
  [TRIGGER-11] agent done: status=ok
  [TRIGGER-12] agent done: status=ok
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: With the flush provider permanently broken (36 consecutive 500s), all 12 user messages still completed with `status=ok` — the death loop is gone. The flush failure is logged rather than delivered as a terminal `run_failed` reply, and the session mapping is preserved/rotated instead of aborting the turn. This is the exact condition that previously produced the permanent loop on `main`.
- **What was not tested**: Live third-party LLM providers (the flush failure is simulated with a deterministic mock 500 to make the path reproducible); long-horizon multi-session persistence across Gateway restarts; and the maintainer-judgment items (session-rotation liveness tradeoff and the opt-in notice semantics) which are product decisions rather than testable code behavior.

target.title: [codex] Keep ambiguous delivery attempts recoverable
target.body:
## Summary

- Keeps outbound delivery entries in ambiguous post-send states pending when adapter reconciliation is unavailable.
- Preserves the existing no-blind-replay behavior while leaving the entry retryable for later reconciliation/backoff.
- Avoids consuming retry budget when no reconciliation-capable adapter ran, so ambiguous entries do not age into terminal failure before a later adapter can reconcile them.
- Treats a reconciliation-capable adapter returning `null` as a completed unresolved reconciliation attempt, so that path still consumes retry budget and respects the max-retry cap.
- Updates startup recovery, reconnect-drain, and outbound queue integration coverage plus Discord troubleshooting guidance for #87544.

## Scope

This is a narrow mitigation for #87544 and intentionally does not close the full issue. The broader transcript-to-provider delivery ledger, Discord reconciliation semantics, and UI/API surfacing still need maintainer design.

## Validation

- Automation main refresh (2026-07-06 JST / 2026-07-05 UTC): merged `openclaw/openclaw@c730d8f1f1bbdff08e470b168dce4874d41d95f6` into the PR branch with no conflicts; pushed head `56d84791f92f38ae6b07844211ce0c387de2531a`.
- GitHub pre-refresh state checked: PR was open/ready and mergeable at the previous head, but the branch was 261 commits behind `origin/main`; old CI had `QA Smoke CI` and `checks-node-compact-small-4` failures on stale head `a3b4c97865598e78c6b5f0c5057af508982758ed`.
- GitHub post-refresh state checked: PR head is `56d84791f92f38ae6b07844211ce0c387de2531a`, base is `c730d8f1f1bbdff08e470b168dce4874d41d95f6`, `mergeable=MERGEABLE`, `mergeStateStatus=UNSTABLE` while new CI is pending, `reviewDecision` is empty/null.
- Review threads checked with GraphQL: 4 total, 0 unresolved. Existing connector reviews are `COMMENTED` only and are not treated as approval.
- `gh pr checks 87552 --repo openclaw/openclaw --required --json name,state,bucket,link,workflow`
  - GitHub reported no required checks on the PR branch.
- `git diff --check`
- `node scripts/docs-list.js`
- `node scripts/generate-docs-map.mjs --check`
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue-storage.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue-recovery.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.storage.test.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.recovery.test.ts src/infra/outbound/deliver.queue-integration.test.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.reconnect-drain.test.ts docs/channels/troubleshooting.md`
  - Note: `corepack pnpm format:check ...` was attempted first, but pnpm entered dependency reconciliation and was interrupted after optional package downloads stalled; the direct command above is the exact `format:check` script body.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.storage.test.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.recovery.test.ts src/infra/outbound/deliver.queue-integration.test.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.reconnect-drain.test.ts`
  - 4 files passed, 69 tests passed.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode branch --base origin/main`
  - Clean: no accepted/actionable findings reported.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: ambiguous outbound delivery entries whose platform send may have started must not be blindly replayed, and must remain pending/recoverable without consuming retry budget when adapter reconciliation is unavailable.

Real environment tested: local OpenClaw source checkout on macOS with Node v22.22.3, rebased onto `openclaw/openclaw@c5d34c8376f8aa32744786cae0473c60e39ef444`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: ran a one-off `node --import tsx --input-type=module` terminal proof that invoked the real `enqueueDelivery`, `markDeliveryPlatformOutcomeUnknown`, `recoverPendingDeliveries`, `loadPendingDeliveries`, and SQLite state reader against a temporary OpenClaw state directory. The proof queued an `unknown_after_send` outbound entry, ran recovery with no reconciliation-capable adapter, and failed if `deliver` was called, the entry did not remain pending, or retry budget was consumed.

Evidence after fix:

```text
info: Found 1 pending delivery entries — starting recovery
warn: Delivery entry <redacted-queue-id> delivery state is unknown_after_send; refusing blind replay without adapter reconciliation
warn: Retry failed for delivery <redacted-queue-id>: delivery state is unknown_after_send; refusing blind replay without adapter reconciliation

deliver call count: 0
pending entries: 1
queue row: {"status":"pending","retry_count":0,"recovery_state":"unknown_after_send","last_error":"delivery state is unknown_after_send; refusing blind replay without adapter reconciliation"}
```

Observed result after fix: recovery refused blind replay, did not call the delivery function, kept exactly one pending queue entry, and persisted `status: "pending"`, `retry_count: 0`, and `recovery_state: "unknown_after_send"`.

What was not tested: no live Discord gateway/channel send was performed in this pass. The broader transcript-to-provider delivery ledger, Discord reconciliation semantics, and Control UI/API delivery-state surface remain open under #87544.

target.title: refactor(memory): drop redundant agent-id scoping from qmd collection names
target.body:
## Summary

- **What:** drop the redundant `-<agentId>` scoping from managed qmd collection names. Each agent has its **own isolated qmd index** (`agents/<agentId>/qmd/index.sqlite`), so collection names can't collide across agents — the agent-id suffix adds nothing but hardcodes the agent id into collection identifiers.
- **How:** remove `scopeCollectionBase` (and two now-dead path helpers, `isPathInsideRoot` / `canonicalizePathForContainment`); name default collections by their base (`memory-root`, `memory-dir`), the session collection `sessions`, and extra collections by their explicit name. Reverse the legacy migration to **scoped→unscoped** (`migrateLegacyScopedCollections` / `deriveLegacyScopedName`) so existing per-agent indexes migrate cleanly.
- **Why migration is cheap:** qmd collections are a **rebuildable derived index** (not user data), so the migration drops the stale scoped collection and lets the unscoped one be (re)created + reindexed — no import, no data loss (consistent with this repo's "prefer delete/drop/rebuild over import for cache").
- **Outcome:** stable, agent-agnostic collection names; net **−42 LOC** of production code for the de-scope itself (removes `scopeCollectionBase` + two now-dead path helpers in `backend-config.ts`).
- **Orphan cleanup:** the scoped→unscoped migration is **kind-gated**. Engine-owned collections (`memory`/`sessions`, whose base names are engine-generated and not user-suppliable) are removed even when their pattern has drifted from the current default; user-named (`custom`) collections keep the path+pattern guards and are **never** auto-deleted. Without this, a pattern-drifted legacy engine collection lingered as an orphan and was re-walked + re-embedded by every `qmd update` — a recurring reindex cost the migration otherwise shipped. (Trade-off, stated for transparency: for engine kinds this intentionally drops the prior "a user coincidentally named a collection like a legacy scoped name" guard — safe because those base names cannot be user-supplied; `custom` retains it.)
- **Disambiguated custom-name upgrade (ClawSweeper P1):** when two custom collections share a name, the shipped scoped names disambiguated as `<base>-<agentId>-<n>` (e.g. `notes-main`, `notes-main-2`), but the unscoped probe `deriveLegacyScopedName(<base>-<n>)` is `<base>-<n>-<agentId>` (`notes-2-main`) — so `migrateLegacyScopedCollections` missed the second orphan, and qmd then rejected the new unscoped collection on the same path+pattern, stranding it under the legacy name. `tryRebindConflictingCollection` now confirms the collection qmd names in the add-conflict via `qmd collection show` (the only command that surfaces the path, reusing `enrichLegacyCollectionPath`) and rebinds it when path **and** pattern match; a parsed name alone never removes a collection, so user-owned path guards are preserved.
- **Stacked on #91253 (per ClawSweeper):** the first commit is the path-aware qmd-rebind fix (#91253); the remaining commits are the de-scope, a docs + session-migration-test follow-up, and the kind-gated orphan cleanup. The rebind is **required** for the migration to be safe — without path-aware metadata, an upgraded index holding both a stale *unscoped* collection (old path) and a current *scoped* one could keep the stale unscoped target active; with the rebind folded in, the stale unscoped collection is rebound to the current path. Once #91253 lands, this rebases to drop that first commit.

## Linked context

Closes #91259

Depends on / folds in #91253 (path-aware qmd collection rebind) — the first commit of this PR.

Related: #91265 (an earlier PR toward the same proposal; this one folds in the path-aware rebind so existing scoped indexes migrate safely, adds an upgrade-case regression, and includes live before/after behavior proof).

Requested by a maintainer or owner? No — follows from the proposal in #91259.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

Behavior addressed: managed qmd collection names dropping the redundant `-<agentId>` suffix; existing per-agent indexes migrate scoped→unscoped; and orphaned engine-owned legacy collections are cleaned up.

Real environment tested: (A) a live, self-hosted OpenClaw gateway (macOS), backend `qmd` (`@tobilu/qmd` 2.5.2) running this build, against an agent whose index already held scoped collections; (B) a scratch per-agent index driven by the real `QmdMemoryManager` + the real `qmd` 2.5.2 binary for the orphan-cleanup case; (C) a scratch in-container→host rebind driven by the real `QmdMemoryManager` + real `qmd` 2.5.2 binary (the sandbox-mode transition).

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
```
# (A) live gateway — de-scope migration on an agent with existing scoped collections:
openclaw gateway restart
openclaw memory index --force --agent <agent>
sqlite3 <agent-qmd-index>.sqlite "select name,path from store_collections order by name;"

# (B) scratch index — seed two legacy scoped orphans (drifted pattern), run the engine (cli mode):
qmd collection add <ws>/memory --name memory-dir-<agent> --mask "**/*.txt"   # engine-owned (memory)
qmd collection add <ws>/notes  --name notes-<agent>      --mask "**/*.txt"   # user-owned   (custom)
# then QmdMemoryManager.create({ mode: "cli" }) runs the migration; list collections before/after.

# (C) sandbox-mode transition — seed a collection at a stale in-container root, run the engine:
qmd collection add <root>/home/node/.openclaw/teams/x/workspace --name workspace --mask "**/*.md"
# then QmdMemoryManager.create({ mode: "cli" }) with workspace=<host-root>; `qmd collection show workspace` before/after.
```

Evidence after fix:
```
# (A) live gateway (identifiers redacted):
# BEFORE (scoped names):
memory-root-<agent>   <WS>
memory-dir-<agent>    <WS>/memory
sessions-<agent>      <agent-state>/qmd/sessions
team-library-<agent>  <WS>/library/promoted
team-library          <WS-old>/library/promoted    # orphan duplicate
# AFTER (reindex):
memory-root / memory-dir / sessions / team-library  # all unscoped
# scoped (-<agent>) collections remaining: 0

# (B) scratch index, real qmd 2.5.2 + real engine (both orphans had a DRIFTED pattern):
# BEFORE:
memory-dir-proofagent  Pattern: **/*.txt   # engine-owned (memory)
notes-proofagent       Pattern: **/*.txt   # user-owned   (custom)
# AFTER (engine ran, mode=cli):
notes-proofagent       Pattern: **/*.txt   # LEFT  — user data never auto-deleted
memory-root / memory-dir / notes           # unscoped, engine-created from scratch
# memory-dir-proofagent : 1 -> 0  (engine-owned, removed)
# notes-proofagent      : 1 -> 1  (user-owned, preserved)

# (C) sandbox-mode transition, real qmd 2.5.2 + real engine:
# BEFORE: workspace -> .../home/node/.openclaw/teams/x/workspace   (stale in-container root)
# AFTER (engine ran, mode=cli): workspace -> .../host/workspace    (rebound to host root)
```

Observed result after fix: (A) all managed collections migrated to unscoped names (including `sessions`); `0` scoped collections remained; the prior orphan duplicate (`team-library` + `team-library-<agent>`) collapsed to a single `team-library`. (B) the engine-owned drifted-pattern orphan was removed while the user-owned one was preserved, and fresh unscoped collections (`memory-root`/`memory-dir`/`notes`) were created. (C) a collection pinned to a stale in-container path was rebound to the configured host workspace root.

What was not tested: launching an actual Docker sandbox container — the bind-mount + container-launch plumbing is OpenClaw platform infrastructure, outside this PR's diff. The in-container→host path transition this PR's code performs is proven with the real binary in (C) above and by a unit test (container→host rebind transition, #91253).

Proof limitations or environment constraints: (A) is redacted terminal output from a private fleet (paths/agent/team identifiers removed); (B) uses generic scratch identifiers and is reproducible by any maintainer on `qmd 2.5.2`.

Before evidence: shown inline in (A) above (the pre-reindex scoped names + orphan duplicate).

## Tests and validation

Commands run (clean checkout off `openclaw/openclaw` `main`, re-verified on the current head after the disambiguation fix):
- `pnpm test extensions/memory-core/src/memory` → **444 passed (40 files)**
- `pnpm test packages/memory-host-sdk` → **38 passed (9 files)**
- `pnpm check:test-types` (tsgo) → **clean, 0 errors**
- `oxfmt --check` + `oxlint` on the touched files → clean.

Regression coverage:
- Default + custom collection-name tests now assert the unscoped form.
- The unscoped→scoped migration tests were replaced with scoped→unscoped ones.
- **Upgrade-case regression (addresses the flagged compatibility risk):** an index holding BOTH a stale *unscoped* collection (old path) AND a current *scoped* one at the name switch → asserts the stale unscoped collection is rebound to the **current** path (via the folded-in `collection show` path enrichment), not left active.
- **Kind-gated orphan cleanup:** a rewritten migration-guard test — a `memory`-kind legacy scoped collection with a drifted pattern is now **removed** (genuinely fails against the pre-fix guard), while a `custom`-kind one with a drifted pattern is **left** — plus a contract test asserting every managed collection carries a `kind` (the safety gate depends on it).
- **Disambiguated custom-name upgrade regression:** two custom collections both named `notes` at different roots, with legacy `notes-<agentId>` / `notes-<agentId>-2` seeded in a real-`qmd`-shaped mock (name-only `collection list`, path-bearing `collection show`) → asserts the disambiguated orphan (`notes-<agentId>-2`) is removed and both unscoped collections (`notes`, `notes-2`) bind to their correct roots. Red against the pre-fix conflict path (the orphan is never removed), green after.

Multi-agent note: safe by construction — each agent has its own isolated qmd index, so unscoped names cannot collide across agents.

## Risk checklist

User-visible behavior change? Internal only — qmd collection identifiers (a derived index) change; no user-facing API/config change.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? Migration only: existing per-agent indexes migrate scoped→unscoped on the next `ensureCollections()` (drop stale scoped + recreate unscoped + reindex). No config keys changed.

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? No.

Highest-risk area: the scoped→unscoped migration on existing indexes, and the kind-gated removal of legacy scoped collections.

How is that risk mitigated: removal only ever targets the exact derived legacy name `<base>-<agentId>` for a **desired** collection. For `custom` collections the path+pattern guards remain, so a user-named collection is never auto-deleted. For `memory`/`sessions` the base names are engine-generated and cannot be user-supplied, so the derived legacy name is unambiguously engine-owned; if such a collection is still configured it is simply re-added at the same path/pattern (net-zero, a reindex). qmd collections are rebuildable, so any dropped-then-recreated collection reindexes from source with no user-visible data loss.

## Current review state

Next action: maintainer review.

What is still waiting: CI + review.

Which bot or reviewer comments were addressed: ClawSweeper review findings on #91274 (docs example, session-migration coverage, scoped-duplicate upgrade case, orphan cleanup, and the disambiguated custom-name migration P1 — fixed via the show-verified conflict rebind).

target.title: fix(irc): chunk PRIVMSG on UTF-16 boundary to avoid lone surrogates
target.body:
**Summary:** Long IRC PRIVMSG payloads were chunked on raw UTF-16 indices, so an emoji straddling a chunk boundary was torn into lone surrogates — malformed UTF-8 on the wire and a garbled glyph for the recipient. This chunks on code-point boundaries so surrogate pairs are never split.

## What Problem This Solves

`connectIrcClient` in `extensions/irc/src/client.ts` splits long PRIVMSG payloads into chunks of at most `messageChunkMaxChars` (default 350). The split was a raw `chunk.slice(0, splitAt)` on the **UTF-16 string**. When the split index lands in the middle of an astral character — i.e. between the high and low halves of a surrogate pair (any emoji such as 🙂 `U+1F642`) — the chunk ends with a lone high surrogate and the next chunk begins with a lone low surrogate. That produces malformed UTF-8 on the wire and a broken/garbled emoji on the receiving client.

Trigger: a message of `"xxxxxxxxx🙂rest"` with `messageChunkMaxChars = 10`. The naive split at UTF-16 index 10 cuts the emoji in half (high `0xD83D` | low `0xDE42`).

## Fix

Add `sliceIrcPrivmsgChunk`, which slices on a safe UTF-16 boundary via the shared `sliceUtf16Safe` helper (`openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime`) so a surrogate pair is never split. Edge case: when a single leading code point already exceeds the chunk budget, `sliceUtf16Safe` would return empty; the helper detects a leading surrogate pair and emits it whole (`text.slice(0, 2)`) so chunking still advances instead of looping. `messageChunkMaxChars` is also clamped to a sane `Math.max(1, Math.floor(...))`.

## Evidence

Real IRC send/receive E2E proof, using a local TCP IRC server process and real TCP clients. This is not a `node:net` / `node:tls` mock.

The sender imported the PR branch's real `connectIrcClient` implementation and connected to `127.0.0.1`. A separate raw `net.Socket` IRC client joined the same channel and received the forwarded `PRIVMSG` chunks from the server. The proof forced `messageChunkMaxChars=10` with payload `"xxxxxxxxx🙂rest"`, placing the emoji at the chunk boundary.

```text
IRC PRIVMSG emoji-boundary real TCP E2E proof
[server] server process pid=1924576
[server] READY host=127.0.0.1 port=37955
receiver: real net.Socket client nick=oc_pr_receiver channel=#oc-e2e
[server] recv NICK nick=oc_pr_receiver
[server] recv USER nick=oc_pr_receiver
[server] welcome nick=oc_pr_receiver
[server] recv JOIN nick=oc_pr_receiver channel=#oc-e2e
sender: real OpenClaw connectIrcClient nick=oc_pr_sender channel=#oc-e2e
[server] recv NICK nick=oc_pr_sender
[server] recv USER nick=oc_pr_sender
[server] welcome nick=oc_pr_sender
payload: "xxxxxxxxx🙂rest"
payload codeUnits=15 messageChunkMaxChars=10
send: OpenClaw client sendPrivmsg(...) over real TCP
[server] recv JOIN nick=oc_pr_sender channel=#oc-e2e
[server] recv PRIVMSG from=oc_pr_sender target=#oc-e2e text="xxxxxxxxx" codeUnits=9 loneSurrogate=false
[server] fwd PRIVMSG from=oc_pr_sender to=oc_pr_receiver target=#oc-e2e
[server] recv PRIVMSG from=oc_pr_sender target=#oc-e2e text="🙂rest" codeUnits=6 loneSurrogate=false
[server] fwd PRIVMSG from=oc_pr_sender to=oc_pr_receiver target=#oc-e2e
raw receiver received PRIVMSG chunks: 2
recv chunk 1: "xxxxxxxxx" codeUnits=9 containsEmoji=false loneSurrogate=false
recv chunk 2: "🙂rest" codeUnits=6 containsEmoji=true loneSurrogate=false
check allChunksWellFormed: PASS
check emojiArrivedIntact: PASS
check rejoinedEqualsOriginal: PASS
check usedRealTcpServerProcess: PASS
check usedRealRawSocketReceiver: PASS
check usedOpenClawConnectIrcClient: PASS
[server] cleanup SIGTERM received
[server] cleanup server closed
cleanup: server process killed pid=1924576 signal=SIGTERM exitCode=0
```

Result: each received `PRIVMSG` chunk is UTF-16 well-formed with no lone surrogate, the `🙂` emoji arrived intact in the second chunk, and the raw receiver's rejoined payload exactly matched the original message.

## Tests

`extensions/irc/src/client.surrogate.test.ts` drives the real `connectIrcClient` over a mocked socket and asserts (red before the fix, green after):

- `does not split an emoji surrogate pair across PRIVMSG chunks` — emoji at the budget boundary is not torn; no chunk contains a lone surrogate.
- `keeps a leading emoji whole when the UTF-16 budget is one code unit` — single-code-point-over-budget edge case emits the emoji whole and advances.
- `splits an all-emoji message into whole emoji when the budget is one code unit` — every chunk is well-formed.
- `still prefers a nearby space when splitting long PRIVMSG text` — confirms the existing word-boundary preference is preserved (no regression).

Each test runs the lone-surrogate regex `/[\uD800-\uDBFF](?![\uDC00-\uDFFF])|(?<![\uD800-\uDBFF])[\uDC00-\uDFFF]/` over every PRIVMSG body the client writes.

target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #57775 by keeping `system.execApprovals.get` and `system.execApprovals.set` in the desktop node command policy instead of dropping them after the node host advertises them.

The commands are now eligible during desktop node pairing and preserved on approved reconnects, so `nodes describe` / Control UI can see exec-approval-capable Windows nodes. target.title: fix(update): guard Windows task autostart during package updates
target.body:
## Summary
- disables enabled Windows Scheduled Task autostart while a managed package update replaces the OpenClaw package tree
- covers running, stopped, and unclassified installed task runtimes, including `--no-restart` stopped/unknown cases where the task can still logon-start during replacement
- re-enables only tasks this update actually disabled, before post-core handoff, restart handoff, blocked-update exits, or failed-update exits
- treats omitted `<Settings><Enabled>` in live Task Scheduler XML as enabled, matching native Windows output where enabled tasks are represented by absence of an explicit disabled state
- reports failed `/ENABLE` recovery if service stop fails after autostart was suspended, so the operator is not left with silently disabled logon autostart
- leaves startup-folder fallback installs, unavailable `schtasks`, missing tasks, unreadable XML state, and already-disabled tasks unchanged

Fixes #87993.

target.title: fix: retry loopback probes without device identity after pairing repair
target.body:
## Summary

Fix a gateway probe edge case where a loopback probe with explicit gateway auth can get stuck in a pairing-repair path because the probe eagerly reuses cached device identity.

The new behavior is narrow:

- probe normally first, including cached device identity when available
- if a **loopback** probe with explicit auth fails before connect with a pairing-required repair response
- retry once without device identity, reusing the explicit token/password auth

This keeps the good path for paired device-aware probes, while avoiding repair-loop churn for local self-probes that already have usable explicit credentials.

## Why

I hit this on a dedicated worker Mac where the main `~/.openclaw` state was doing mixed duty:

- unattended worker/node state
- local CLI self-probe state

The dedicated profile gateways behaved fine, but the worker's plain main self-probe could repeatedly trigger device metadata repair requests instead of just using the explicit local gateway auth it already had.

That produced a noisy and misleading failure mode for `openclaw gateway probe` on loopback.

## Change details

- add a targeted retry path in `src/gateway/probe.ts`
- only trigger that retry when all of these are true:
  - loopback URL
  - explicit probe auth is present
  - a cached device identity was attached
  - the first attempt fails in `pairing_pending` with `PAIRING_REQUIRED`
  - failure happens before a successful connect/hello
- add a focused regression test in `src/gateway/probe.test.ts`

## Validation

Ran:

NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192 pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts src/gateway/probe.test.ts
```

target.title: fix(infra): tolerate deleted cwd across startup, PATH, home-dir, and TUI [AI-assisted]
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #73676. If a shell's working directory is removed before OpenClaw starts, Node's `process.cwd()` throws `ENOENT: uv_cwd`. CLI dotenv/PATH bootstrap and TUI startup used that call directly, so `openclaw tui` terminated before it could render a useful interface.

## Why This Change Was Made

Introduce one small nullable-CWD primitive, then keep the decision at each owner boundary:

- dotenv skips the vanished workspace file and continues global loading;
- PATH setup skips the opt-in project-local bin lookup rather than substituting HOME;
- required-home resolution uses valid configured sources or fails with actionable guidance;
- TUI workspace inference skips a missing cwd, autocomplete/auth use the package-root fallback, and local `!` commands refuse instead of silently running somewhere else.

This maintainer rewrite removes the redundant `is-main` refactor, the extra helper/test-routing surface, and the long fallback comments from the contributor patch. Normal cwd-present behavior is unchanged.

## User Impact

The CLI and full-screen TUI can start after their launch directory has been deleted. Security-sensitive project/PATH and local-shell semantics do not gain an implicit fallback. The unrecoverable no-home/no-cwd edge case now names the environment variables or directory action required.

target.title: improve(auto-reply): render chat history since last reply as per-message prose
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a readability problem where the "Chat history since last reply" prompt block delivers replayed channel history to the model as a raw JSON array of `{sender, timestamp_ms, message_id, body}` objects. The sibling chat-window block already renders the same kind of entries as per-message prose (`#id [time] sender: body`), so the same conversation currently reaches the model in two different shapes inside one prompt, and the JSON form buries who-said-what in field syntax. In busy multi-party rooms this weakens sender attribution when the model reasons over replayed history.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuses the existing `formatChatWindowMessage` renderer for the history block so both blocks share one prose shape. The untrusted framing label (`Chat history since last reply (untrusted, for context):`) is unchanged, media stays redacted (a bare content-type tag such as `[image/png]`, never local paths or URLs, matching the previous JSON form's redaction), and the inbound-metadata stripper learns to consume the prose form of the block. History selection, bounding, and chat-window dedup logic are untouched; only the rendering of entries changes.

## User Impact

Agents replaying group-channel history now see lines like `#m-1 09:38 Alice: hello` instead of a JSON dump, which reads the same as the chat-window block and improves sender attribution in multi-party channels. No configuration change and no new options.

## Evidence

Before (fixture, abbreviated):

```
Chat history since last reply (untrusted, for context):
[
  {
    "sender": "Alice",
    "timestamp_ms": 1736380700000,
    "message_id": "m-1",
    "body": "<media:image> (1 image)",
    "media": [{ "kind": "image", "content_type": "image/png", "has_local_path": true, "has_url": true }]
  }
]
```

After (same fixture):

```
Chat history since last reply (untrusted, for context):
#m-1 09:38 Alice: <media:image> (1 image) [image/png]

target.title: feat(logbook): automatic work journal plugin with Control UI timeline tab
target.body:
Closes #99867

## What Problem This Solves

There is no way to look back at a day and see what you actually did on your machine. Time trackers log app names; they miss what the work was. Dayflow (MIT, standalone macOS app) proved the recipe — periodic screen capture, vision-model observation, timeline synthesis — but as a separate app its output is locked away from the assistant.

This PR adds **Logbook**, a bundled (disabled-by-default) plugin that turns screen snapshots from a paired node into a reviewable timeline of the day, surfaced in a new Control UI sidebar tab, with a daily-standup generator and timeline-grounded Q&A.

## Why This Change Was Made

OpenClaw already owns every capability the idea needs — node screen capture, media-understanding providers, plugin services, gateway RPC, plugin SQLite state, the dashboard. Composing them as a plugin keeps the data local, makes it queryable by the assistant later, and exercises existing seams:

- **Capture**: a plugin service invokes `screen.snapshot` (app nodes) or the new plugin-provided `logbook.snapshot` node-host command (headless macOS node hosts, backed by `screencapture`/`sips`) every `captureIntervalSeconds` (default 30s). A node-invoke policy adds `logbook.snapshot` to the default macOS allowlist while the plugin is enabled. Identical consecutive frames are marked idle and excluded from analysis.
- **Two-stage analysis** (Dayflow-style): elapsed windows (default 15 min, split at >2 min gaps) go to a structured-extraction vision model (`api.runtime.mediaUnderstanding.extractStructuredWithModel`, e.g. `codex/gpt-5.5`) producing timestamped observations; observations plus a 45-minute lookback of existing cards are revised into 10-60 min timeline cards via `api.runtime.llm.complete` (default agent model), with one JSON-repair retry. Cards are a revisable draft: later batches may restructure the recent window.
- **Storage**: plugin-owned SQLite (`node:sqlite`, same pattern as memory-core/imessage) under `<state-dir>/logbook/`; frames pruned after `retentionDays` (default 14); batches stuck in `running` reset to `pending` on restart.
- **UI**: new `Logbook` tab following the Workboard/Dreams precedent (core view calling plugin-registered `logbook.*` gateway methods; plugin-disabled callout when off). Timeline cards with category colors, keyframe snapshots, distraction chips; day stats; standup generator; ask-your-day box.

Architecture notes: owner boundary respected (all product logic in `extensions/logbook`; the core diff is generic tab wiring + i18n). No new core config; plugin config has 8 clamped keys. Raw SQL is plugin-local DDL plus prepared statements, matching existing extension storage (the shared Kysely helpers are core-only).

## User Impact

- Off by default; no behavior change until `openclaw plugins enable logbook`.
- Once enabled: the Logbook tab shows the day as expandable activity cards with focus/category stats, one-click standup notes, and natural-language recall over the tracked day.
- Privacy: frames and the timeline stay on the gateway host; images leave only as analysis input to the operator-chosen model; the headless capture command is only advertised/allowlisted while the plugin is enabled.

## Evidence

- Unit tests: `extensions/logbook/src/analyze.test.ts` (time parsing, JSON repair contract, overlap trimming, batch windowing/gap split, sampling, keyframe pick) and `extensions/logbook/src/store.test.ts` (idle exclusion, crash recovery, revision-window replacement, stats, retention pruning) — 21 tests green via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/logbook`.
- Contract suites green: `src/plugins/contracts/package-manifest.contract.test.ts`, `src/plugins/contracts/extension-runtime-dependencies.contract.test.ts`, `src/plugins/bundled-plugin-naming.test.ts`, `test/extension-import-boundaries.test.ts`.
- `pnpm build` green (bundled plugin dist + control UI assets); `pnpm tsgo` + `pnpm tsgo:extensions` green; scoped oxlint green; `pnpm ui:i18n:sync` regenerated locales.
- **Live end-to-end on macOS** (isolated-state dev gateway + headless node host from this branch): node paired with `logbook.snapshot` in its approved surface; real screen frames captured every 10s (19+ frames, idle detection active); analysis batches ran against real `codex/gpt-5.5` (`chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses` transport) producing timestamped observations and merged timeline cards that correctly described the on-screen work; the Logbook tab rendered cards with keyframe snapshots, day stats (focus bar, categories, apps), a generated Daily Standup (Done/Today/Blockers), and an answered ask-your-day question. Live-test screenshots contain personal screen content and were reviewed locally instead of being attached.
- The live test also hardened the plugin: node-invoke policy allowlisting, `node.invoke` payload-envelope unwrapping, node-inventory diagnostics in capture errors, and config-snapshot loading for the tab were all found and fixed against the running gateway.

Release-note context: feat(plugins): add Logbook automatic work journal plugin with Control UI timeline tab (screen snapshots via paired nodes, Dayflow-style two-stage analysis, daily standup, ask-your-day).

target.title: fix(feishu): route chat tools through contextual accounts
target.body:
﻿Related: #96657

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where multi-account Feishu users could run `feishu_chat` from the wrong configured account.

`feishu_chat` covers the `info`, `members`, and `member_info` actions. Those actions are account-sensitive because chat IDs, member IDs, and visible membership data belong to the Feishu app/tenant that can access them. Before this PR, chat registration checked only the first enabled account and every chat client was created from that same account, so execution context such as `agentAccountId: "b"` could still call Feishu through account `a`.

This caused two concrete failures:

- a contextual chat call for account `b` could use account `a` when both accounts enabled chat;
- `feishu_chat` could fail to register when the first account disabled chat even though a later enabled account allowed it.

This PR is intentionally narrower than #96657. It only aligns `feishu_chat` with the existing Feishu tool-account resolver and does not claim to fix every non-inbound Feishu routing path.

## Why This Change Was Made

`feishu_chat` now follows the same resolver pattern as neighboring Feishu tools: registration checks whether any enabled account exposes chat, and execution creates the client through `createFeishuToolClient` with the current tool context.

The Feishu API calls, request payloads, response shape, configured secrets, and required Feishu/Lark scopes are unchanged. The account precedence is explicit: `accountId` parameter, then contextual `agentAccountId`, then the existing resolver fallback.

## User Impact

Single-account Feishu setups keep the same behavior.

Multi-account setups now route chat/member lookups through the selected contextual account instead of silently using the first enabled account. If the selected contextual account has `tools.chat` disabled, the tool fails closed with the existing disabled-tool error instead of falling back across accounts or tenants.

## Evidence

Focused regression coverage verifies:

- contextual `agentAccountId` selects the matching chat account;
- explicit `accountId` overrides the contextual account;
- disabled contextual chat accounts fail closed;
- chat registers when only a later configured account enables chat.

Redacted live/staged proof was gathered on 2026-06-30 with two local Feishu/Lark profiles managed by `lark-cli`. Secrets, access tokens, open IDs, chat IDs, tenant keys, group names, and member names were not included in the PR.

```text

- profile a: bot identity ready, chat get returned expected chat fields
- profile b: bot/user identities ready, chat list/get returned expected chat fields

staged OpenClaw production-router check:
- registeredFeishuChat: true
- contextAgentAccountId "b" -> selectedAccount "b"
- contextAgentAccountId "a" with account a chat disabled -> failedClosed true
- errorClass: Feishu Chat tools are disabled for account "a"
```

target.title: fix(heartbeat): skip plugin bootstrap and bundled fallback during delivery target resolution
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a heartbeat wake-loop latency regression where delivery-target resolution blocks for ~60s per tick when the configured channel plugin is not already in the active runtime registry.

### Background

Commit [`6470bb7625`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/6470bb7625) (fix(heartbeat): bootstrap plugin session targets, #93630) solved a real problem: when a user configured `heartbeat.target` to a channel id that was not in the built-in known-deliverable-channel list (e.g. a third-party plugin id), `normalizeDeliverableOutboundChannel()` returned `undefined` and the target was silently dropped to `"none"`.

The fix called `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin({ allowBootstrap: true })` in the heartbeat delivery-target path. However, this triggers `resolveRuntimePluginRegistry()` → `loadOpenClawPlugins()`, which scans **all** installed plugins — not just the target channel.

### Root cause analysis

The `bootstrapOutboundChannelPlugin` guard in `channel-bootstrap.runtime.ts` has a `bootstrapAttempts` Set that caches per `(registryVersion, channel)` key:
- **Successful bootstrap**: key stays cached → subsequent ticks skip instantly
- **Failed bootstrap** (plugin not installed / config issue / transient failure): key is deleted → every tick re-runs the full plugin scan

This is the pathological case: a misconfigured or not-yet-installed heartbeat plugin channel causes repeated ~60s scans on every wake tick. The probe measurement confirmed:

```
Before (allowBootstrap: true,  no plugin): 73,308ms
After  (allowBootstrap: false, no plugin):   5.2ms
Pre-activation bootstrap (cold scan):           739ms (once at startup)
```

### When this bug is triggered

1. `heartbeat.target` is not `"none"` or `"last"`
2. The target channel is not in the active runtime registry
3. `heartbeat.to` is set (non-empty)

## Why This Change Was Made

Two-part fix:

### Part 1: Hot path optimization (original PR)

Three heartbeat-path call sites in `targets.ts` now pass `allowBootstrap: false, allowBundledFallback: false`. A new `allowBundledFallback` parameter is added to `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin` (default `true`) so hot paths can skip both the bootstrap scan AND the `getBundledChannelPlugin` lazy-load fallback.

### Part 2: Startup pre-activation (new — addresses review feedback)

A new `preactivateHeartbeatChannelPlugins()` function in `src/infra/outbound/heartbeat-pre-activate.ts` runs **once at gateway startup** (in `activateGatewayScheduledServices`, before `startHeartbeatRunner`). It reads the heartbeat config and, for non-standard plugin channel targets, calls `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin({ allowBootstrap: true })` to load the plugin into the active registry before the wake loop starts.

This preserves the delivery compatibility that PR #93630 established — external plugin channel heartbeat targets still get bootstrapped — but moves the bootstrap cost from the hot path (every tick) to startup (once).

Standard deliverable channels (telegram, discord, etc.) and targets of `"none"`/`"last"` are no-ops in pre-activation.

## User Impact

- **Normal deployment (plugin active)**: No change — plugin found in registry, <10ms resolution both before and after
- **Plugin not yet active** (external channel, delayed activation): Pre-activation resolves it at startup (~135–739ms once) instead of every heartbeat tick (~60s each). Delivery works.
- **Plugin not installed / misconfigured**: Fast fail at startup (best-effort bootstrap) and fast fail on hot path — no repeated scans

## Compatibility

- `allowBundledFallback` defaults to `true` — all non-heartbeat callers unchanged
- Pre-activation is a no-op for standard channel targets and `target: none/last`
- `resolveOutboundTarget` (general-purpose outbound) continues to pass `params.allowBootstrap` through transparently

## Evidence

### Unit tests (92/92 passed)
```
src/infra/outbound/targets.test.ts                  85 passed
src/infra/outbound/heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts    7 passed
```

### Probe timing (isolated vitest)
```
Pre-activation bootstrap (cold scan):  739ms (external-channel)
Pre-activation bootstrap (cold scan):  135ms (plugin-channel)
Hot path (allowBootstrap: false):       <10ms (registry lookup)
```

### Lint / type checks
```
oxlint:  clean
tsgo:    clean (check:test-types)
format:  clean (oxfmt --check)
build:   clean (pnpm build)
```

### Review response

ClawSweeper review ([#100377](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100377#issuecomment-4886719486)) identified that removing bootstrap from the hot path could drop delivery for external plugin channels not yet in the active registry. Startup pre-activation addresses this by resolving those plugins once before the wake loop starts, preserving the delivery compatibility of #93630 while keeping the hot path free of plugin scans.

target.title: fix(security): suppress unhandled stdout/stderr stream errors in install policy
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`runPolicyCommand` attaches `data` listeners to `child.stdout` and `child.stderr`, but does not attach `error` listeners. If either stream emits an `error` event, the unhandled error can crash the process or leave the policy command hanging.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add no-op `error` handlers to both stdout and stderr streams before the data handlers, mirroring the existing stdin error handling pattern. This prevents unhandled stream errors from propagating as uncaught exceptions.

## User Impact

More robust install policy execution: transient stream read errors no longer crash the OpenClaw process during skill/plugin installs.

## Evidence

- Added a regression test in `src/security/install-policy.test.ts` that mocks `spawn`, emits `error` events on both stdout and stderr, and verifies `runInstallPolicy` still resolves successfully.
- Verified the test fails on `main` with an unhandled `Error: stdout read failed` and times out, and passes with this fix.
- `oxlint` passes on the changed files.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where cron-driven embedded agent runs could appear completed even when the final assistant turn produced no deliverable reply, leaving the configured channel without a response or failure signal.
